title: Dispatch CUS 9: City Keeps a Record of Its Unbuilt Neighbors
summary: The census is complete, though two valid maps survive in the archive.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: The municipal census has been certified with a supplementary schedule for Fenwick Lane and Vesper Row. The main total counts Alderwick as it stands; the schedule records the households whose streets were planned here but built in another arrangement of the city.

Mr. Reed has filed both maps under the rejected improvement scheme of 1887. The other city’s plan is not marked as a correction to ours. Miss Morrow has placed Miss Hume’s signed acknowledgment beside it, so later officials will know why the streets appear in the census but not on Alderwick’s paving.

Inspector Voss removed the last braces from North Loom Street yesterday. The bookshop wall is solid. Mr. Keene says a visitor who never saw the doorway would find nothing remarkable there. He has pressed Mrs. Keene’s violet between the pages of a volume she once gave him in this city.

Dr. Saye cannot say whether the paired entries created a boundary or allowed one to close. She says a census usually answers where people live. This one required its registrars to admit that two families could live at the same numbered place without either family being a mistake.

The first eviction notices are preserved with the volumes. Across each printed order, Miss Morrow has written the date it was cancelled. She says that is part of the record too: no one had to leave for either city to remain their home.
